title: When People Ate Mummies as Medicine

sections.name: When People Ate Mummies as Medicine
lines: For hundreds of years, Europeans ate dead people as medicine. Specifically, Egyptian mummies.
Mummies were ground into a powder called mumia, and sold in apothecary shops.
People mixed it into drinks to treat bruises, headaches and almost anything else.
It may have started with a translation mix up. Mumia was originally a word for a natural black tar used as medicine.
Demand got so high that some sellers made fake mummies from recently dead bodies.
The trend only faded in the 1700s. Today, mummies go to museums instead of medicine cabinets.
